title: A stale index beside an input is refused and named
body:
When `sail` reads an input through its index, `index_of` in `input.rs` checks `index::is_current`. If the `.saidx` beside the file is missing or stale, it builds a fresh `Index` in memory and writes nothing. `sail skim`'s `total()` falls back to a counting pass the same way. A stale index file therefore costs a full scan on every run, and nothing tells the user.

sail-978552 decided that a stale part of an aggregate index is refused and named. This brings the single-file case in line.

## Proposal

- A `.saidx` that exists beside the input but does not describe it as it is now is an error that names the index file and says to run `sail index` again or delete it. `is_current` returns `false` for a stale stamp, an unreadable file and another version alike, so all three refuse.
- A missing `.saidx` is unchanged. `--read auto` picks the indexed backend for positional and counted operations whether or not an index exists, and builds the offsets in memory when none does.
- Only commands that would consult the index refuse. `--read stream` and `--read memory` never read it, except `sail skim`, whose streaming arm reads its count from a current index.

## Cost

A change to what `sail` does. A run that succeeded with a stale index now fails. It goes under `### Changed` in `sail`'s changelog. `libsail` does not change.
close_reason: Landed in 216d1f0 on dev. sail count and sail names never read the index file and are tracked in sail-fe4c0a.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/424f83e5
notes.text: Built on dev, not yet committed. `current_index` in `input.rs` is shared by `index_of` and `sail skim`'s `total()`. The CLI test is `an_index_of_the_file_as_it_was_is_refused_and_named`, run against `cat --read indexed`, `get` and `skim --read stream`. `names` and `count` never read the index file, so they do not refuse. That is filed separately.
